AFP PHOTO / ALEXANDER JOE The 83-year-old, who guided Brazil to the 1994 FIFA World Cup title, will continue his recovery and medical care at home. CHENNAI Former Brazil head coach Carlos Alberto Parreira, who guided the national team to its 1994 FIFA World Cup triumph, was discharged from hospital on Saturday following a three-month stay caused by a serious lung infection during his cancer treatment.

news.title: Modric available to play for Croatia in Nations League
news.lede: FILE PHOTO: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - Round of 32 - Portugal v Croatia - Toronto Stadium, Toronto, Canada - July 2, 2026 Croatia's Luka Modric acknowledges fans after the match as Croatia are eliminated from the World Cup REUTERS/Jeenah Moon/File Photo. Sept 5 - Luka Modric is still available to play for Croatia, the country's soccer association (HNS) said on Saturday, ending speculation that the veteran midfielder would end his international career after this year's World Cup. Croatia captain Modric, who turns 41 on Wednesday, has been playing for the national team since 2006, earning over 200 caps and helping them reach the 2018 World Cup final.

news.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino makes an appearance at U20 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has arrived at the opening of the Under-20 Women’s World Cup as he faces continuing pressure since abandoning his plan to sell off World Cup profits. Infantino was seen in the stands speaking with Polish football federation president Cezary Kulesza as host nation Poland faced Argentina on the opening day of the tournament on Saturday. Infantino had mostly kept out of the spotlight in the weeks since his World Cup sell-off plan fell apart amid opposition from many Fifa member nations and some of his own officials. The European nations – a quarter of the 24-team field – backed down on a boycott threat last week, citing assurances from Fifa that the plan would not be revived.

news.title: FIFA President Infantino To Attend U-20 Women's World Cup Opener In Katowice
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino will make his first public appearance at the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Katowice following the controversial abandonment of his $20 billion World Cup commercial rights sale proposal. FIFA President Gianni Infantino will attend the opening match of the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Katowice on Saturday, the first tournament organised by world football's ruling body since his abandoned proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup. The Swiss administrator called off the plan, which valued the commercial rights of the World Cup and other FIFA tournaments at $20 billion, in late July in the face of a fierce backlash from regional governing bodies including Europe's UEFA and major stakeholders in the sport. A spokesperson for the Polish Football Association confirmed the embattled Infantino would be at the opening game.

news.title: Gianni Infantino to attend FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup opener in Poland
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino will attend the opening match of the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup in Katowice, Poland, on Saturday, September 5. The Polish Football Association has confirmed his presence for the game between hosts Poland and Argentina.Poland have been drawn in Group A alongside Argentina, Mexico and Benin. They will face Mexico on September 8 before finishing their group campaign against Benin on September 11. The 2026 tournament is the 12th edition of the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup and will feature 24 teams.

news.title: Infantino Set for U-20 Women’s World Cup Opener Amid FIFA Controversy
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino will be in the spotlight when the U-20 Women’s World Cup gets underway in Poland on Saturday, just weeks after he was forced to abandon a controversial proposal involving the commercial rights to FIFA’s biggest tournaments. Infantino is expected to attend the opening match in Katowice, where Poland will face Argentina, as the world football governing body begins another edition of its youth women’s competition. A spokesperson for the Polish Football Association confirmed the FIFA president’s attendance, with about 15,000 spectators expected for the first two matches of the tournament.
